criteria.limit_once: Restrict the row-limit number to one PARAM token while the top-level LimitCount names that reference. Further sightings invalidate the descriptor, confining the call-provided LIMIT figure to its clause.
criteria.limit_shared: Ask only that the top-level LimitCount name the row-limit reference, leaving other PARAM tokens free to repeat the number. Each occurrence takes the identical LIMIT binding without further scrutiny.
criteria.review_needed: Neither limit rule follows from this evidence, or neither one meets the contracts.

limit_exclusivity.instructions: Settle whether the row-limit number belongs to LIMIT alone or tolerates additional parameter positions. Rely on common and topics.limit_exclusivity.

criteria.allow_trivia: Treat a solitary RawStmt as sufficient and retain all outer semicolons, remarks, and spacing verbatim inside segments. Console-derived text needs no cleanup.
criteria.clean_ending: Treat a solitary RawStmt as sufficient only absent ASCII_59, SQL_COMMENT, and C_COMMENT tokens opening on or past the termination of the last other token. Leading matter stays; trailing semicolons and remarks invalidate.
criteria.review_needed: Neither trivia rule follows from this evidence, or neither one meets the contracts.

trailing_semicolon.instructions: Settle whether trailing semicolons and remarks endure or invalidate. Rely on common and topics.trailing_semicolon.

fixed_constraints: P12 standardizes one statement per descriptor: SELECT with the row-limit parameter as top-level LIMIT for one/optional/many; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE minus RETURNING for execute. Application parameters pack $1..$N alongside parameter-record fields in sequence, then the row-limit parameter as N+1. Scanner displacements slice fixed bytes into template fragments; a duplicate SQL lexer is forbidden.

Manifest checks already fix row_limit_parameter to len(parameters)+1 on row-returning descriptors and outlaw it on execute. canlc examines descriptors once per compilation; the sealed findings serve I35 lowering, where LIMIT values derive from max_rows or 2.

Proven server reactions on PostgreSQL 17.11 through Bun 1.4.2 extended protocol: terminal semicolons, terminal gaps, and terminal remarks execute; dual statements fail with cannot insert multiple commands into a prepared statement; a LIMIT numeral filtering elsewhere executes under one shared binding.

Upstream measurement facts: RawStmt StmtLen stays 0 without a terminal semicolon, so scanner tokens delimit statements. Semicolons tokenize as ASCII_59, commentary as SQL_COMMENT or C_COMMENT, and SELECT 1 trailed by semicolons remains a single RawStmt.
common.purpose: Counsel Can solely on the proof enclosed below. Skip research, coding, and explanation. Wherever the proof leaves options tied, select the designated uncertainty result.

limit_exclusivity.facts: P12 designates the top-level LIMIT the distinct parameter behind the application parameters. Under parameters [term] with limit 2, limiting purely on $2 spends the I35 call-site amount a single time. Filtering on $2 as well steers that identical call-site amount into selection without warning. Servers accept both layouts; compile rules alone separate deliberate choice from mistake.

trailing_semicolon.facts: Practitioners import SQL bearing terminal semicolons and commentary from live sessions. Servers stomach all such trailing material yet still bar authentic multi-statement payloads. A stricter gate only shrinks admissible static text; execution safety holds either way because fragments conserve bytes and bindings stay native.
